newsitem.title: USA: Oklahoma defense lawyer says documents stolen.
newsitem.headline: Oklahoma defense lawyer says documents stolen.

text.p: The attorney for Oklahoma City bombing defendant Timothy McVeigh said Monday documents used as the basis of a story claiming his client had confessed were stolen, but those documents did not represent a confession.
"It isn't a confession by Tim McVeigh," Stephen Jones told a news conference. "It wasn't then. It isn't now."
Jones declined to explain what the document was or how it was used by the defence.

The Dallas Morning News reported Friday via the Internet that McVeigh had admitted planting the bomb that exploded at the Alfred P. Murrah federal building in April 1995, taking the lives of 168 people.
Jones did not say exactly how the documents had been stolen other than by breaking into the defence team's computer.
On Monday, the newspaper said it would publish no new articles based on confidential defence documents.
Jones also said he did not yet know if he would need to seek a change of venue from Denver. He also said he might have to ask for a 90-day continuance of the March 31 starting day for the trial.
"A lot will depend on the next 24 to 48 hours," Jones said.
